Current analysis, step by step

  • Read corrected tail angles and timing. Use each fish’s corrected angle frames, camera timing, stimulus protocol and angular-validity coverage. Check the source hashes. Frame times follow the constant camera cadence inferred from stable arrival runs.
  • Calculate raw vigor before detecting bouts. Sum the 16 tail-angle components, calculate the wrapped change between consecutive valid frames, take its absolute value and divide by the inferred time step. The raw signal is angular speed in radians/ms; this is a framewise quantity, not a bout median.
  • Detect bouts from raw vigor. Apply the shared median smoothing and rolling-envelope detector, then the amplitude, duration and interbout-gap rules. Bout detection occurs before calculating any bout summary; it is identical in all three versions.
  • Keep eligible moving samples and take the natural logarithm. Require valid consecutive frames, a finite detector envelope, at least 80% angular tail coverage, membership in a detected moving bout, and finite positive raw vigor. Other samples are missing contributions.
  • Align each trial to CS onset. Display trials 5–94 within [−20, +20) s. Pre = trials 5–14; Train = 15–64; Test = 65–94.
  • Construct the value to display. C and D sample versions replace each bout’s eligible log samples by their median within that trial’s displayed 40 s window. Version 2 instead averages the direct eligible log samples inside each 0.5 s bin; it does not substitute bout medians.
  • Calculate a separate baseline for each trial. In [−15, 0) s, obtain P10, m = P50 and P90 from eligible samples for the sample versions, or from finite bin means for Version 2. Quantiles use linear interpolation. In the sample versions, longer eligible bout durations supply more baseline samples; in Version 2 each finite baseline bin votes once.
  • Centre, scale and clip. Subtract m. C divides by half the P10–P90 range; D divides by the larger distance from m to P10/P90, using the same denominator for both signs. Clip the result to [−1, +1]. A missing or zero denominator makes the trial’s display values undefined.
  • Render the heatmaps. Use one shared managua_r colourbar labelled “Vigor relative to baseline,” thin boxed axes, white phase boundaries, time ticks at −20/0/+20 s and phase names on the right. Sample rectangles preserve eligible sample durations without filling gaps; Version 2 has 80 half-second cells per trial.
Detector settings used in all versions

Median window: 10 ms (7 samples). Rolling maximum: 28.57 ms (21 samples); rolling minimum: 571.43 ms (401 samples). Envelope threshold: 4°/ms; raw peak threshold: 1°/ms; minimum bout duration: 57.14 ms; maximum interbout gap: 14.29 ms. Rolling windows require finite support; invalid-frame gaps are not bridged.

Interpretation: zero is that trial’s baseline median. Positive/negative colours indicate higher/lower log vigor on the chosen relative scale. Black indicates missing contributions or an undefined scale, not zero or confirmed immobility. H trial 16 has an undefined scale in all three rows.

What changes between the versions?

VersionValue before centringBaseline voting unitDenominator
Version 1 · CBout median log vigor on each eligible sampleEligible sample(P90 − P10) / 2
Version 1 · DSame bout median and sample intervalsEligible samplemax(m − P10, P90 − m)
Version 2 · CMean of direct eligible log samples per 0.5 s cellFinite baseline-bin mean(P90 − P10) / 2

All baselines use [−15, 0) s; m = P50. C versus D isolates the denominator change. Version 1 versus Version 2 changes the bout summary, temporal aggregation and baseline weighting together. D cannot have a larger absolute value than C for the same centred sample; the two coincide when the baseline quantile distances are equal.

Version 1 C remains the selected processing freeze. D and Version 2 C are additional reviews. Version 2 uses C, consistent with the original comparison; a D-bin figure has not been generated.
